title: review: R19: spawn.extract_json prefers a fenced JSON block or the last balanced object, so a reviewer's prose containing braces no longer voids its verdict
spec:
Why: spawn.extract_json (orchestrator/spawn.py:646-652) slices from the first '{' to the last '}' in the worker's final message. Reviews T-0583 and T-0587 today wrote prose such as `hold_reason=f"merge {status}"` before a fenced ```json {"verdict":"approve",...} ``` block, so the slice started inside the prose, json.loads failed, and both approvals were recorded as "review returned no parseable verdict" (the Planner transcribed them by hand). The review prompt now forbids prose, but the parser must still be robust.
What (orchestrator/spawn.py extract_json only, behaviour-preserving for plain JSON):
1. If the text contains one or more fenced blocks (``` or ```json ... ```), try json.loads on each fenced body, last one first; return the first dict that parses.
2. Otherwise scan for balanced top-level {...} objects (respecting strings and escapes), try json.loads from the last candidate backwards; return the first dict that parses.
3. Otherwise keep today's behaviour: slice first '{' to last '}' and fall back to {"summary": text[:2000], "parse_error": True} (or {"summary": text[:2000]} when no brace exists).
Tests in tests/test_spawn.py as unittest.TestCase methods (this repo runs unittest).
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_extract_json_prefers_fenced_block_after_prose_with_braces — prose containing f"merge {status}" followed by a fenced json block returns the fenced object with verdict approve
tests/test_spawn.py::test_extract_json_falls_back_to_last_balanced_object — no fences, prose with a stray '{x}' then a valid object returns the valid object

tests/test_spawn.py::test_extract_json_plain_object_and_parse_error_unchanged — a bare JSON object is returned as before; text without any parseable object returns summary plus parse_error True; text without braces returns summary only
